ai.description: This 1-meter sea snake has a pale blue-grey body with black bands and a distinct brown upper lip. It features a paddle-like tail and lacks the enlarged belly scales found in terrestrial snakes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Laticauda laticaudata* is uniquely identified by the presence of a distinct, dark brown or blackish band crossing the snout, which is absent in other Indian sea kraits.
ai.habitat: The Brown-lipped Sea Krait inhabits tropical coastal waters and coral reefs, frequently seeking shelter in rocky crevices and mangrove forests along the shoreline.
ai.behavior: The Brown-lipped Sea Krait is primarily nocturnal, emerging from the ocean at night to hunt for eels among coral reefs before returning to land to rest and digest.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Laticauda laticaudata* is oviparous, laying clutches of 2–10 eggs on land. Breeding occurs year-round, with peak activity often observed during the monsoon months.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Brown-lipped Sea Krait inhabits the coastal waters and islands of the Indian subcontinent, specifically along the eastern coast and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
